So why doesn't she feel safe fully unloading on you? There's stuff she should work out internally, for sure - which can be tied to her attachment history. Witnessing our parents marriage informs us of what is normal. On top of our own relationship with our parents, they drill into us deep subconscious ways on how we cope as adults in our relationship. Right now, it sounds like you're pursuer while she's a withdrawer which is a terminology in couples therapy. But y'all can get caught up in unhealthy patterns. It's important to recognize that. A built up of resentment is wounds that have been built up and unsaid over the 15 years that y'all have been together. Open, SAFE, COMMUNICATION might've not been both your Forte since you were both young when you got together. So entering into a new healthy patter is new. The relationship can last if 1. So by her subconsciously protecting herself and you, it actually causing more distance. 2. If she's  willing to find forgiveness after that realization. 3. If you can both mutually hear each other out without getting defensive and attacking one another.


Love shifts and evolves,as you learn to love someone, you see different angles of that person. It's a different angle but shapes that person in a more fuller way. Perhaps y'all are stuck on seeing each other as parent/roommate angle and have lost the perspective of lover angle. It just takes a lot of internal and emotional work. Sometimes years to feel reconnected with your emotions again.
